title: RESCUE HF-CS:  A study comparing istaroxime with placebo in patients with cardiogenic shock caused by acute heart failure
official: A randomized, double-blind, phase 2b/3 clinical study of istaroxime combined with standard care versus placebo and standard of care for the treatment of early cardiogenic shock (CS)  due to acute heart failure (AHF)
summary:
Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of istaroxime continuous infusion (plus standard of care) relative to placebo (plus standard of care) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) due to AHF on decreasing short-term symptom (dyspnea) severity.

To assess whether patients with CS due to AHF achieve greater clinical benefit with istaroxime than with placebo continuous infusion (on top of standard of care) with respect to mortality, need for invasive circulatory intervention, morbidity, and health-related quality of life.
conditions: Cardiogenic shock (CS) due to Acute heart failure.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged between 18 and 80 years old (inclusive) at the time of informed consent, regardless of gender.
2. Diagnosed with CS due to AHF during screening, before randomization, and meeting all of the following criteria: a.	Dyspnea at rest or with minimal activity before screening and randomization. b.	Pulmonary rales, or lower limb edema by physical examination. c.	Evidence of pulmonary congestion by chest X-ray, CT scan or lung ultrasound  d.	At the time of screening and just prior to randomization either:  1)	systolic BP ≤ 100 mmHg or  2)	systolic BP ≤ 115 mmHg and >100 mmHg accompanied by at least one sign of hypoperfusion or hemodynamic compromise: cool extremities, oliguria, elevated lactate (>2 mmol/L), worsening renal function attributable to low perfusion, or invasive/noninvasive hemodynamic evidence of reduced cardiac output.
3. Initial hospitalization (defined as first medical contact in the hospital) for this AHF event within 20 hours before randomization.
4. Documented history within 6 months prior to screening, or during the current admission, of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40%.
5. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) > 1,500 pg/mL or BNP > 400 pg/mL during screening, before randomization.
6. Signed informed consent as described in Section 11.3 which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF) and in this protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Body weight < 40 kg or ≥ 150 kg at Screening.
2. Severe valvular stenosis that has not been surgically corrected, or moderate or severe aortic regurgitation
3. Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or restrictive cardiomyopathy, constrictive pericarditis, cardiac tamponade, cardiomyopathy based on infiltrative disease (such as amyloidosis), accumulation disease (such as hemochromatosis, Fabry disease), myocardial dysplasia, cardiomyopathy caused by reversible causes (such as stress cardiomyopathy) or acute myocarditis
4. Sustained ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation within 30 days of screening and randomization.
5. Significant bradycardia (sustained ventricular rate <50 beats per minute), or second or third-degree atrioventricular block (except those using permanent pacemakers).
6. Type 1 acute coronary syndrome (ACS)/myocardial infarction (MI) in the 30 days prior to screening inclusive of the current admission.
7. Patients who have undergone percutaneous coronary angiography or coronary artery bypass grafting or other major cardiovascular surgery including ICD and / or CRT or mechanical support devices within one month before screening, or patients who are expected to require revascularization within three months after screening.
8. Patients on mechanical circulatory support (MCS) or who require sedation and mechanical ventilation during Screening or at the time of randomization.
9. Patients who are expected to require heart transplantation or left ventricular assist during the study period.
10. Patients diagnosed with malignant tumors within 1 year before signing the informed consent form or at the time of screening (excluding fully treated cervical carcinoma in situ, basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, localized prostate cancer after radical surgery, and breast ductal carcinoma in situ after radical surgery), or those undergoing anti-tumor treatment at the time of screening.
11. Patients with diseases that in the opinion of the investigator may lead to mortality within 90 days from randomization
12. Rapidly deteriorating cardiogenic shock requiring escalating support
13. Patients who suffer from severe mental or psychological disorders, cognitive impairment, or a history of mental illness. Patients with mental illness (such as depression) who can independently consent can be enrolled in the current study.
14. Patients with known severe allergies or a history of severe drug or food allergic reactions, or those known to be allergic to Istaroxime or its ingredients including lactose.
15. Patients who are pregnant, breastfeeding or planning pregnancy.
16. Patients who cannot be guaranteed to take effective contraceptive measures from the time of signing the informed consent to the 30 days following their last exposure to study drug, or who are of childbearing potential and plan to donate sperm/eggs during this period.
17. Patients of childbearing potential without a negative highly sensitive serum pregnancy test within 24 hours before the first dose of trial intervention.
18. Patients participating in other clinical studies and/or received other study intervention (study drugs or medical devices, etc.) within 30 days before signing the informed consent form, or who are still in the follow up period of other clinical studies.
19. Patients who are unable to comply with all study requirements.
20. Any other circumstances deemed by the investigator to be inappropriate for conducting this study.
21. Patients with any systolic blood pressure measurement >130 mmHg within 2 hours prior to randomization.
22. Administration during the 6 hours prior to screening of vasodilators such as nitroglycerin, nitrates, recombinant human brain natriuretic peptide
23. Received digoxin within 7 days before randomization
24. Taking a CYP2C19 substrate (refer to Appendix in Section 12.2)
25. Patients with severe lung disease (dependent on oral steroids or immunosuppressive therapy or require home oxygen therapy), respiratory failure, or severe pulmonary hypertension
26. Acute ischemic or hemorrhagic cerebral infarction or transient ischemic attack within 30 days before screening
27. Abnormal laboratory findings including during screening: a.	Renal impairment (eGFR < 25 ml/min/1.73 m2) or the need for long-term or intermittent renal support therapy (hemodialysis, ultrafiltration or peritoneal dialysis); b.	Severe electrolyte imbalance (Na+ <120mmol/L or >160mmol/L, and/or K+ <3.2mmol/L or >5.5mmol/L); c.	Liver function impairment (ALT and/or AST > 3 times the upper limit of the normal range and/or bilirubin exceeds 1.5 times the upper limit of the normal range); or d.	Hemoglobin <9 g/dL (<5.6 mmol/L).
